title: Decouple kernel-ranking heuristics and traffic fences to prevent misalignment during capacity ramps
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: After a capacity ramp on 2025-02-18 we observed a sustained p95/p99 latency regression for a subset of hosted customers. Root cause analysis shows correlated shifts in kernel-ranking scores produced by the heuristic layer plus aggressive probe traffic from the scheduler; together these caused repeated misassignment of requests to suboptimal kernels and KV cache warmup thundering. This ticket tracks follow-up work to decouple ranking signals from transient probe spikes, introduce traffic fences during ramp, and harden rollout safety gates.
timeline: 2025-02-18 03:12 UTC: Scheduled capacity bump for us-east-1; autoscaler activated new workers.
2025-02-18 03:15 UTC: sudden rise in kernel-probing rate observed from scheduler (x4 baseline).
2025-02-18 03:17 UTC: p95 latency increased from 78ms -> 240ms on affected cluster; error rates remained low.
2025-02-18 03:45 UTC: Ops mitigated by rolling back recent scheduler probing config; partial improvement but instability remained.
2025-02-19 11:00 UTC: Post-incident triage started; trace correlation shows repeated kernel reselection and KV cache miss amplification.
2025-02-20 09:00 UTC: Root-cause hypothesis finalized: heuristic score amplification + probe bursts -> eviction and cold KV cache -> tail latency.
2025-02-20 15:00 UTC: Decision to implement short-term traffic fencing + medium-term heuristic dampening and signal decoupling.
investigation_notes: Heuristic scoring uses recent microbatch success and kernel latency estimates; a burst of probes inflates short-term success signal and biases ranking toward recently probed kernels.
Scheduler probing increased 4x during ramp due to a mis-tuned backoff parameter introduced in runtime-1.23 which assumed stable capacity—this interacted poorly with autoscale spin-up.
KV cache warmup baseline showed >70% miss rate for kernels that received sudden high probe traffic, causing token re-computation overhead and microbatch requeueing.
Telemetry indicates kernels with fused-attn paths were more sensitive because their initial probe path bypassed a late-stage caching layer, increasing cold-start penalty.
Anecdotal repro on staging using synthetic ramp reproduced p99 tail with same pattern when probe_rate_multiplier > 2.
repro_steps: 1) Stand up a 3-node inference cluster on staging with runtime-1.23 candidate image.
2) Configure scheduler probe_rate_multiplier to 3 and enable autoscale to add nodes after 2m ramp.
3) Drive synthetic load with realistic sequence length distribution; measure kernel assignment churn and KV miss ratio.
4) Observe that within 90s of ramp, kernel-rank score variance increases and p99 latency spikes by >=2x.
5) Toggle heuristic dampening feature flag to confirm mitigation reduces churn and tail latency.
action_items: Short-term: Add traffic fence that caps probe_rate_multiplier to 1.5 during autoscale ramps (owner: Liam O'Connor, due: 2025-02-25)
Short-term: Temporarily revert mis-tuned backoff change in runtime-1.23 probe policy (owner: Sofia Mendes, due: 2025-02-24)
Medium-term: Implement decoupling of short-window probe success signal from persistent kernel rank (introduce EWMA with dampening) (owner: Arun Patel, due: 2025-03-12)
Medium-term: Add KV-cache warmup pacing to avoid thundering by staggering probe payloads across nodes (owner: Mei Chen, due: 2025-03-15)
Medium-term: Add canary gating on scheduler probe multiplier changes with automated rollback if kernel-assignment-churn > 5/min (owner: Priya Kapoor, due: 2025-03-18)
Long-term: Rework heuristic feature flags to enable A/B evaluation of ranking signals and automated metric-driven rollouts (owner: Runtime Platform team, due: 2025-04-30)
Monitoring: Create dedicated dashboard tile for kernel score entropy and KV warmup impact (owner: Observability, due: 2025-02-28)
rollout_plan: Stage 1 (short-term fences): deploy a config change to scheduler in us-east-1 only; monitor p99 and choreograph with SRE (target: canary 1h).
Stage 2 (heuristic dampening): feature-flagged rollout to staging -> canary cluster -> 25% production over 24h with automated rollback on pre-defined guardrails.
Stage 3 (KV warmup pacing): enable with conservative pacing on small percentage of traffic; validate KV-hit improvement and latency improvement before broader rollout.
If any stage increases error rates or latency outside guardrails, immediately rollback and open hotfix PR.
test_plan: Unit tests for EWMA dampening math and config boundaries.
Integration tests on staging with synthesized ramp traffic and assertions for kernel-assignment-churn < 2/min.
Chaos test: simulate slow worker startup while autoscale ramps to verify fence prevents probe amplification.
Load test with production-like prompt mix to verify KV warmup pacing reduces initial p99 by >=30%.
risks: Over-dampening heuristics could delay beneficial kernel migrations leading to suboptimal throughput.
Staggered warmup may increase initial load on certain nodes if pacing is misconfigured.
Feature-flag complexity increases risk of configuration drift across clusters.
